destination.name: Victor Harbor
destination.tagline: Whales, penguins and a horse-drawn tram on South Australia's Encounter Bay coast
destination.description: Victor Harbor is a seaside town on Encounter Bay on the southern Fleurieu coast, built around a foreshore and the causeway to Granite Island. A horse-drawn tram crosses the causeway to the island, where little penguins breed and a walking trail circles the coast. Southern right whales come close to shore in winter, and the town has a whale centre and a free clifftop platform on the Heysen Trail. The sheltered bay at Port Elliot and the Bluff headland are a short drive east and west.
whyVisit: Watch southern right whales from shore
Ride a horse-drawn tram to an island
Walk the coast to sheltered bays

goodToKnow.title: Whale season
goodToKnow.detail: Southern right whales are usually seen from June to October, so winter is the time to scan the bay from the foreshore or a lookout.

goodToKnow.title: Free island entry
goodToKnow.detail: Entry to Granite Island Recreation Park is free. Horse-drawn tram rides and guided tours are run separately and charged on top.

goodToKnow.title: Waterfall timing
goodToKnow.detail: Hindmarsh Falls runs strongest in winter and spring, which suits a combined day with whale watching.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Southern right whales visit in {months}, and Hindmarsh Falls runs fullest in the same wetter season.
